title: Run it, break it, read the trace
about: Every line of code in this film is read from examples/plugged-in, and every line of terminal output is replayed from docs/manual/captures, recorded by running the commands for real.

lines.text: Everything is green. So you try it yourself, and something looks wrong.
ortho dev runs the app on your machine, with a local world. No cloud account.
lines.say: Ortho dev runs the app on your machine, with a local world. No cloud account.

lines.text: Plugged In has no screens yet. So we use the command line tool that was generated from the blueprint.
Aaron claims a name: first page. It answers with a handle's id.
Then he claims a second name.
Refused. A code, HN-002, and a name: handle already owned.
lines.say: Refused. A code, H N zero zero two, and a name: handle already owned.

lines.text: Is that a bug? You don't have to know. You say what you saw: I asked for a second name, and it said no. And you hand that to your agent.
The agent doesn't guess, and it doesn't open the handler. It makes the same call again, and keeps one thing from the answer: the trace's id, in a header.
Then one command. ortho telemetry trace, with that id.
lines.say: Then one command. Ortho, telemetry, trace, with that id.

lines.text: The trace is everything that one call did. Read the first line. The operation. How long it took. And the word refused, with the refusal's name.
The next line is the cause. A rule, by its name in the blueprint: one name per person.
And look at what's missing. The record step ran. There is no commit. The rule was checked after the work, and before anything was saved.
Beside it, a call that was answered. Its last step is the commit.
So the refusal didn't come from the handler at all. It came from six lines of blueprint.
A person holds one claimed name at a time. Unique on the owner, while the handle is claimed. Refuse with: handle already owned.
From what you saw on screen, to the line that gave it, in two commands.
Now the question is yours, and it's a real one. Should a person hold only one name?
If yes, the app is right, and the message needs work. If no, you change the rule, and that's a later chapter.
Two things to watch for. Refused means a declared answer, with a code. A defect is the server failing, and it's marked as one. Don't read one as the other.
And if an explanation doesn't name a line of the blueprint, ask for the trace.
Two parts are missing today. No command signs a test person in to a local app, so the recording asks the local world's own door. And the generated tool doesn't print the trace's id.
